item.title: Underwater Acoustic Communication: An Introductory Guide to Modulation
item.author: huangxu2024@shanghaitech.edu.cn (Xu Huang)
item.description:
Why acoustic communication?
#

Underwater acoustic communication is the technology that uses sound waves to carry information through water. Electromagnetic waves (radio, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) attenuate extremely fast in seawater — practical ranges are usually a few meters at most. Sound, by contrast, propagates hundreds of meters to tens of kilometers in the ocean, making it the only practical wireless medium underwater. The field has been developing for over a century, from early underwater bell navigation to modern underwater sensor networks.

item.title: Acoustic Communication and Positioning for Untethered Underwater Robots
item.author: huangxu2024@shanghaitech.edu.cn (Xu Huang)
item.description:
Why acoustics?
#

Radio waves (2.4 GHz Wi-Fi/Bluetooth) penetrate only a few centimeters in seawater. Optical links reach tens of meters at Mbit/s rates but require a clear line of sight and fail in turbid water. Sound, however, propagates kilometers through seawater without a line of sight and requires relatively simple hardware. Once an underwater robot operates untethered, command, telemetry, and navigation must all travel acoustically.
